SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Ms. Emerson Specimen is a 47-year-old female who reports onset of low back pain on 06/18/2026. She describes the pain as aching, localized to the lumbar region, worsened with prolonged sitting and forward flexion. Low back pain began on 06/18/2026. She denies any trauma or neurologic symptoms.
She reports trying over-the-counter acetaminophen with minimal relief.
Exam: Vital signs normal. Inspection shows no deformity. Palpation reveals tenderness over paraspinal muscles L3-L5. Range of motion: forward flexion limited to 60 degrees due to pain, lateral bending and rotation mildly restricted. Straight leg raise negative bilaterally. Neurologic exam: strength 5/5 bilaterally in hip flexion, knee extension, and ankle dorsiflexion; reflexes 2+ at patella and Achilles; sensation intact to light touch in lower extremities.
Assessment: Acute lumbar strain, likely muscular.
Plan: Start NSAID therapy; ibuprofen 600 mg PO q6h PRN, started today 06/19/2026. Prescribe a course of physical therapy to begin in 3 days focusing on core stabilization and lumbar flexion exercises. Advise activity modification, ice/heat as needed. Return in 2 weeks or sooner if worsening.

SYNTHETIC – NOT A REAL PATIENT
HPI: Patient returns for follow-up after 3 weeks of conservative management. She reports low back pain persisting, unchanged in character. NSAID therapy was started on 06/19/2026 and ended on 07/27/2026 with partial response. Physical therapy was initiated on 06/22/2026, completed 10 sessions by 07/27/2026, and showed no improvement.
Exam: Vital signs stable. Lumbar paraspinal tenderness persists. Range of motion: forward flexion 50 degrees, lateral bending 20 degrees each side. Straight leg raise negative. Neurologic exam: strength 5/5 hip flexion bilaterally, 4/5 left great toe extension (motor weakness consistent with L5 radiculopathy). Reflexes: diminished left ankle jerk, otherwise 2+ patellar. Sensation decreased to light touch over left lateral foot.
Assessment: Objective radiculopathy findings include diminished ankle reflex and L5/S1 weakness.
Plan: Continue NSAIDs as needed for symptom control. Recommend home exercise program. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings. She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

Assessment: Ongoing lumbar radiculopathy L5/S1.
Plan: NSAID therapy was started on 06/19/2026 and ended on 07/27/2026 with partial response. Physical therapy was initiated on 06/22/2026, completed 10 sessions by 07/27/2026, and showed no improvement. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings. She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.

HPI: Patient returns for pre-surgical evaluation; low back pain persists despite NSAID and PT.
Exam: Unchanged; neurologic exam shows 4/5 left great toe extension and diminished left ankle reflex.
Assessment: Lumbar radiculopathy L5/S1 with objective findings.
Plan: Lumbar MRI ordered today 08/03/2026 to further evaluate disc pathology. Spine surgery referral is under consideration pending MRI findings. She denies fever, weight loss, trauma, cancer history, bladder or bowel incontinence, saddle anesthesia, or progressive neurologic deficits.
